correctness.rationale: The proof establishes a global candidate-set reduction via strict monotonicity of sinh(beta u)/sinh(alpha u), a unique horizon from the increasing ratio of two exponential deficits, and a distinct Hessian threshold in the slope-balanced case. The symbolic special case and independent finite stress tests agree; the latter are supplemental, not proofs. The derivative-ratio sign law and monotone (1-exp(-alpha T/2))/(1-exp(-beta T/2)) prove all quantifiers. Under b beta=a alpha the midpoint Hessian changes sign at T_loc; the fourth derivative is strictly negative at equality, endpoints are inward strict local minima, and T_loc<T_* follows from strict global classification.
